source.title: Diffusion Soup: Model Merging for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
source.authors: Benjamin Biggs; Arjun Seshadri; Yang Zou; Achin Jain; Aditya Golatkar; Yusheng Xie; Alessandro Achille; Ashwin Swaminathan; Stefano Soatto

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses and evaluates shard-removal unlearning for text-to-image diffusion models, but does not test whether targeted knowledge is forgotten or recovered by any attack in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports general image-quality metrics after removing data shards and measures memorization-related image distances. These do not measure recovery of targeted knowledge by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting, nor whether targeted knowledge accuracy reaches chance. The shard-removal results below are recorded as related findings with versions none.
record.test_reason: Diffusion Soup removes data shards from averaged text-to-image diffusion weights. It reports only general image quality (TIFA, Image Reward, CLIP) after removal. It never measures whether the removed shard's knowledge is gone, and it runs no recovery attack: no fine-tuning, internal edit, quantization or prompting. So it tests none of versions A–F. Exact-subtraction shard removal is also a different construct from the approximate LLM unlearning the claim concerns.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present weight averaging as training-free continual learning and unlearning by shard subtraction. They report negligible general-quality loss on removal and argue souping reduces memorization. They do not evaluate whether removed content is truly forgotten or can be recovered.
record.recipe_differences: The method averages weights of text-to-image diffusion models trained on data shards and subtracts a shard to remove it. It does not use the LLM unlearning methods or evaluate the recovery attacks named in the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting one domain-specialist shard from a uniform diffusion soup keeps general quality: at most 1% IR drop, and TIFA/CLIP close to the full soup (Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact shard subtraction from a diffusion weight soup preserves general image quality. Whether the shard's content is forgotten is not measured.

record.problems: The unlearning evaluation reports general image-quality outcomes rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy or attack-based recovery. Individual leave-one-out chart values are not given in the text, and uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional shard-removal rows extracted: Figure 4 shows individual leave-one-out values for TIFA, IR, and CLIP, but the text provides only the aggregate IR statement and qualitative summaries. The study does not report outcomes relevant to any claim version.

untested.parts: Forgetting of targeted-shard content and resistance to attacks. Only general quality is reported.
No activation ablation and no deletion-versus-blocking analysis.
No robustness claim against recovery attacks is evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: Different domain: diffusion models with exact compartmentalized removal. The anti-memorization CLIP-distance results concern memorization of training images, not recovery after unlearning, and correctly have no rows.

versions.untested_parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy after unlearning and recovery under simple attacks; the reported metrics are general image quality.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether unlearning deletes knowledge versus blocking access.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
The paper does not evaluate resistance to the attacks listed in the claim.

rows.subject: Diffusion Soup (uniform soup)
rows.operation_detail: Remove one specialist shard from the weight soup by weighted subtraction.

conditions.value: domain specialist shards; one removed at a time

rows.value: After removal, at most 1% lower; .45 → .44, as stated in the abstract
rows.note: The text reports the result across shard removals; Figure 4 displays the individual leave-one-out results. This is general image quality, not targeted-knowledge forgetting or recovery.
rows.check: This is a general-quality retention metric (IR .45 to .44 after shard removal), not targeted forgetting or recovery. 'observed' has no meaning against any version. Note that .44 is the Greedy soup value in Table 1, but the text does state .45 to .44 for removal.
